Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated GPU qualification & ops on-ramp

Hi Amit —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so you and your team have a single place to pick up next week. High-level notes and confirmation items below.

Summary of pain and goals
- Latency spikes with long-tail (p99 > 400ms) during peak inference for your clinical triage model; this is impacting throughput and user experience.
- Data isolation requirement: PHI-adjacent inputs, so you need tenant isolation with dedicated lanes and audit logs.
- Predictable throughput for batch processing windows and burst during morning surge.
- Target: p50 ~ 40–60ms, p99 < 150ms for sync generation; 99.9% uptime SLA for inference endpoints.

Recommended starting commitment (subject to technical validation)
- Initial reserved pool: 8x A100-class GPUs (dedicated pool). We recommended a dedicated pool to meet isolation + throughput goals.
- Canary: 2 GPUs (isolated) for staged rollout and performance validation.
- Scaling plan: add capacity in 4-GPU increments with automated burst to shared capacity if short on reserved headroom.

Technical considerations we heard
- Model size: 13B family (FP16/INT8 experiments). Need to validate KV cache sizing and memory for S-Attention patterns.
- Quantization: potential to reduce footprint; want to preserve quality for clinical prompts.
- Ops: need audit logs for inference requests, key rotation (KMS), and longer retention for logs (90 days).

Next steps and owners
- Redwood to share an ops runbook template + preliminary cost estimate (action: Soojin) — deliver by Fri 2026-05-22.
- Medion to share sample traffic profile and a redacted prompt set for eval (action: Amit / Sana) — target next Tue 2026-05-26.
- Ben to propose a canary test plan and guardrails for quantization experiments (action: Ben) — draft by Mon 2026-05-25.
- Procurement intro & timelines: Amit to loop procurement contact (Cc'd) and confirm expected billing terms.

Attachments included: ops-runbook-template.xlsx (runbook skeleton), medion-procurement-contact.vcf (contact card).

If anything above is incorrect or missing, flag it and I'll update immediately. Otherwise I'll circulate the runbook and cost sketch by Friday.

Best,

— Soojin

- The team expects to run nightly batch jobs that are latency-insensitive (can be queued) and daytime interactive workloads that need the p99 SLA.
- For the canary, we'll initially run a small subset of traffic (approx 5% of traffic) to validate response quality and latency.
- Procurement timeline: we typically need ~3–4 weeks for contract review. I'm looping Sana (engineering lead) and procurement so they can weigh in on technical and billing constraints.

Hi all — quick technical note and proposed canary plan: 

Technical clarifications:
- For a 13B family model with expected sequence lengths ~512 tokens, 8x A100 gives comfortable headroom for concurrency of ~60–80 concurrent short requests with batching. We'll validate with your traffic sample.
- KV cache sizing: plan for a dedicated 128GB of cache across hosts; we'll instrument metrics to ensure we don't evict under load.

Proposed canary (2-GPU isolated pool)
- Duration: 1 week internal validation + 1 week limited production (5% traffic).
- Metrics to validate: latency p50/p95/p99, token-level cost, generation quality (prompt set eval), error rates and cold-cache behavior.
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to hosted-mix model if p99 > 250ms or error rate exceeds 0.5% for >5m.

I will draft the canary test checklist and share the link here once ready. Also flagging quantization: we'll run INT8 for batch jobs first, AB test against FP16 for quality.

— Ben
